summary: Delivered release identity (#337), cursor-key independence (#340), permission-aware readiness (#344) and the pepper runbook/rehearsal (#434) were audited and re-run on a clean candidate. All local Cloudflare runtime evidence passes. Production activation was NOT PERFORMED; no production secret was set or rotated, and no production resource was contacted.

classification.runtime: workerd through @cloudflare/vitest-plugin 1.4.0 with local D1, Durable Object SQLite and R2 bindings
classification.credentials: synthetic fixture credentials only; every command ran with a minimal environment (HOME, PATH, LANG, TERM) so no agent-session identity or Cloudflare credential variable was inherited
classification.faked_transport: external OIDC discovery/JWKS fetches only; authentication, authorization, minting and lookup run production code
classification.limits: Does not prove production secret propagation, provider availability, consumer rollout, live installation rebinding, or the deployed production release.

observations: Audit observation, not a confirmed blocker: no step among the release scripts this audit read (release-validate, release-pack, release-verify, release-smoke) asserts that the Worker bundle embedded in the compiled CLI carries BUILD_COMMIT equal to manifest.revision. This audit checked v0.8.0 by inspection. The release worker is to corroborate it independently before it is treated as a gap.
generate-version.mjs records git HEAD even when the working tree is dirty; the release path is protected by release-validate.mjs requiring a clean checkout, a local development build is not.
GET /api/runtime/info advertises io.tila/durable-conversations unconditionally. It is protocol support, not configured readiness; readiness is the conversation route response.

behavior_observed: Existing scoped (including DPoP-bound) tokens and legacy cookie sessions are rejected after the pepper changes, while human account sessions are unaffected; an interrupted owner session is recovered through the independent infrastructure token.
A lost rotation response is recoverable from a fresh inventory; the superseded token id returns 409.
Rollback restores unrevoked old credentials but never a revoked one.

Pre-cutover invitations are rejected under the new pepper yet remain pending; a restored pepper makes them redeemable again, as do transition-issued invitations when the new pepper is re-applied. Invitations revoked through the owner endpoint stay unusable. The Worker has no automatic guard, so revoked/expired state is an operator prerequisite in the runbook.
Conversation send/read and an outstanding cursor keep working across the cutover with the dedicated key held constant.
criteria.still_open_gate: An authorized production maintenance execution, which is not requested here. This rehearsal does not make the pepper migration a prerequisite of enabling conversations.

runbook_corrections: docs/05-OPERATIONS.md: replaced the false statement that no public invitation-revocation endpoint exists. Owners list invitations (GET /projects/:projectId/runtime/invitations) and revoke them (POST /projects/:projectId/runtime/invitations/:invitationId/revoke); the SDK, CLI (tila machine invitations, tila machine revoke-invitation) and dashboard use them.

docs/05-OPERATIONS.md: rollback and re-application require every invitation issued before or during the cutover to be read back as revoked or expired. A rejected redemption, a listing entry, or an absent local value is not proof.
docs/05-OPERATIONS.md: the invitation inventory comes from the owner listing, not retained setup values; invitations last 10 minutes.

docs/05-OPERATIONS.md: conversation enabling (CONVERSATION_CURSOR_KEY) is separated from credential migration (HASH_PEPPER) and the fallback coupling is stated: with neither secret, setting HASH_PEPPER also turns the routes on.
docs/05-OPERATIONS.md: the targeted rehearsal command needs the generated version file on a fresh checkout.
docs/05-OPERATIONS.md: the cursor-key command names the verified Worker; health and runtime info are not readiness evidence.
docs/13-MULTI-INSTANCE-AUTH.md: pending invitations revive with a restored pepper.

risks: The invitation revival is real product behavior with no server guard; safety depends on the operator following the runbook prerequisite.

The revocation prerequisite needs a deployment that has the owner invitation listing and revoke routes and D1 migration 0034 (the invitation_id backfill). The CHANGELOG lists the routes under 0.8.0 and the commit that added migration 0034 is contained in no earlier tag (git tag --contains); the routes were not separately bisected. A deployment without them cannot satisfy the prerequisite and must be upgraded and migrated first.
Unconfirmed audit observation: the embedded-Worker BUILD_COMMIT assertion gap described under release_identity_audit.observations awaits independent corroboration by the release worker.
redaction: No credential, token, cookie, password, recovery link, secret value or private host address is recorded. Fixture values in the tests are synthetic and are not reproduced here.
